## 1. Identification Strategy  

Primary design: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study lead/lag specification, augmented by an Instrumental-Variables (IV) first stage that predicts highway placement with plausibly exogenous geographic instruments.

Why DID?  
• The National Trunk Highway System (NTHS) opened different links in different years between 1998-2007, creating time-series plus cross-section variation.  
• Annual regional panels exist for the whole period.  
• The question is “what happens to a region after it gains highway access relative to similar regions that have not yet (or never) gained access?”—classic DID.  

Why IV augmentation?  
• Route planning was not purely random; richer or more politically connected regions could have been prioritized.  
• We therefore instrument actual highway access with a planner-cost, topography-based “least-cost” route surface that was calculated ex-ante and is orthogonal to contemporary economic shocks.

Estimation sequence  
(1) First stage: predict HighwayAccess_it using geographic instruments Z_i.  
(2) Second stage: regress outcomes on predicted access using two-way FE DID.  
(3) Event-study on the same instrumented treatment to test parallel trends and dynamic effects.

Packages: fixest (felm-style IV) and did or did2s for modern staggered-DID inference.

------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Treatment and Control Definition  

Treatment variable  
HighwayAccess_it = 1 if the centroid of region i is within 10 km of an NTHS segment that is operational in year t. (Robustness: 5 km, 20 km buffers; inverse-distance treatment intensity.)

Timing / Event date  
TreatYear_i = opening year of the first segment that activates HighwayAccess=1.  
“Event time” k = t – TreatYear_i.

Control group  
• Never-treated regions, plus not-yet-treated regions in years prior to their TreatYear_i.  
• If concerned about differential pre-trends, nearest-neighbor propensity-score or synthetic-control weights within DID.

Instrument (for IV step)  
Z_i = 1{predicted least-cost corridor passes within 10 km of region i} based on:  
   – Straight-line connections between pre-1990 provincial capitals,  
   – Minimized construction cost computed from 90-m SRTM elevation and slope,  
   – No economic covariates.  
This is time-invariant and predetermined.

------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Parallel trends: Absent the highway, treated and control regions would have followed the same trajectory in industrial outcomes.  
• Plausibility: China’s industrial policy was centrally set, but growth differed across coast/interior. We include province-year FE and test with event-study leads.

A2. Exogeneity of instruments: Geographic least-cost corridors affect outcomes only through actual highway construction.  
• Plausibility: Elevation and slope are unrelated to late-1990s productivity shocks after controlling for geography FE and controls.

A3. No anticipatory behavior: Firms do not relocate in advance of the official opening date.  
• Plausibility: Construction dates were uncertain; still, we will include two to three leads to test for pre-treatment effects.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): One region’s treatment status does not change the counterfactual outcomes of another (no large spillovers).  
• Plausibility is weaker—trade corridors create spillovers. We will test by excluding regions within 50 km of treated units (“donut”).  

A5. Monotonicity (IV): The instrument weakly increases the chance of being treated (no “defiers”).  
• Plausible because being on the predicted corridor cannot reduce the probability of road construction.

------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Main Threats & Mitigation  

1. Endogenous route placement  
   – Mitigation: IV with geographic instrument; control for 1990 log GDP, population, distance to prefectural capital, historical roads.  

2. Differential pre-trends (especially coast vs. inland)  
   – Mitigation: Province-year fixed effects; allow region-specific linear trends; event-study to test equality of ‑5 to ‑1 leads.  

3. Spatial spillovers / market re-sorting  
   – Mitigation:  
     a. Cluster SEs by contiguous-region group.  
     b. “Donut” sample: drop regions within X km of treated.  
     c. Aggregate to broader labor‐market areas and check sign/size.  

------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. R Code Outline  

```r
# Load packages -------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(sf)          # for spatial treatment construction
library(fixest)      # fast TWFE with IV
library(did)         # event-study for staggered DID
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data loading -----------------------------------------------------------
reg <- fread("region_panel_1998_2007.csv")   # panel with outcomes
roads <- st_read("nths_segments.shp")        # GIS shapefile with open_year
regions <- st_read("regions.shp")            # polygons or centroids

# 2. Construct treatment ----------------------------------------------------
# (a) find first year each region is within 10 km of an opened segment
roads_buf <- st_buffer(roads, dist = 10000)  # 10 km buffer

regions$region_id <- as.integer(regions$region_id)
treat_year <- sapply(regions$region_id, function(r){
  yrs <- roads$open_year[st_intersects(regions[regions$region_id==r,], roads_buf, sparse=FALSE)]
  if(length(yrs)==0) return(Inf) else return(min(yrs))
})

regions$treat_year <- treat_year

# merge into panel
reg <- merge(reg, 
             regions |> st_drop_geometry()[,.(region_id, treat_year)],
             by="region_id")

reg[, treated := as.integer(year >= treat_year)]
reg[is.infinite(treat_year), treated := 0]  # never treated

# Event time
reg[, event_time := ifelse(is.infinite(treat_year), NA, year - treat_year)]

# 3. Construct instrument ---------------------------------------------------
# same least-cost corridor spatial join already pre-computed:
instr <- fread("instrument_leastcost.csv")   # region_id, Z
reg <- merge(reg, instr, by="region_id")

# 4. Baseline IV-DID --------------------------------------------------------
# Industrial outcome (log)
est_iv <- feols(log_ind_output ~ 1 | region_id + year | 
                   (treated ~ Z), data = reg, cluster = ~province_id)
summary(est_iv)

# 5. Event-study with IV pre-treatment leads --------------------------------
library(did2s)   # Gardner 2022 method
reg[, rel_time := ifelse(is.infinite(treat_year), NA, year - treat_year)]
reg <- reg[rel_time > -6 & rel_time < 8]     # window

event_iv <- did2s(yname = "log_ind_output",
                  first_stage = treated ~ Z,
                  D = "treated",
                  idname = "region_id",
                  tname = "year",
                  data = reg)
summary(event_iv)

# 6. Robustness: narrower buffer (5 km) ------------------------------------
# Re-run treatment construction with 5 km and replicate IV-DID
```

------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Expected Results  

Direction: Positive—improved market access should raise industrial output and employment.  
Magnitude (prior): Within 5 years, a treated region could see roughly a 6–10 percent increase in real industrial output and a 3–5 percent rise in manufacturing employment relative to controls.

------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID/IV)  

C1. Clear treatment timing & staggered adoption .............. 1  
C2. Parallel pre-trends supported by event-study ............. 0.8 (pending test)  
C3. Exogenous instrument validity (exclusion restriction) .... 0.7  
C4. No large spillovers ...................................... 0.5  
C5. Correct inference (clustering, staggered DID) ............ 1  

Overall = 4.0 / 5 → “generally credible but spillovers and instrument validity need scrutiny.”
